question.text: SEBI has broadly classified mutual fund schemes into how many categories?

answer.text: 5 categories — Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Solution Oriented, and Others
3 categories — Equity, Debt, and Hybrid only
4 categories — Equity, Debt, Hybrid, and Index funds
6 categories — Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Commodity, Currency, and Others

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI has broadly classified mutual fund schemes into 5 categories: Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Solution Oriented, and Others. Under each category, SEBI has further defined specific sub-categories with defined asset allocation norms. Only one scheme per category is permitted (with exceptions for index funds/ETFs, Fund of Funds, and sectoral/thematic funds). The Trap: Many candidates forget about "Solution Oriented" and "Others" categories. Index funds fall under "Others," not as a separate main category. Commodity and Currency are not separate SEBI MF categories. Cross-Exam Context: MF topics overlap with Series V-A, V-B. The SEBI categorization framework is a heavily tested topic in all MF-related NISM exams. Distributor's Pro-Tip: This SEBI categorization ensures uniformity — investors can compare similar schemes across fund houses. Use this framework to help clients understand what type of fund they are investing in and whether it matches their goals.
